subject: HBM bottleneck duration + U.S. localization: SK hynix expects shortage through end-2030
body_md:
Thesis: the AI-memory bottleneck is broadening from a generic capacity story into a dated, geography-specific HBM supply-chain constraint. SK hynix says its >$4B Indiana advanced-packaging facility will begin next-generation HBM mass production in H2/Q3 2029, while CEO Kwak Noh-Jung told Reuters he expects the current memory shortage to persist through end-2030. The site is intended to connect Korean wafer production with U.S. packaging/testing and U.S. customers. This strengthens—but does not replace—the existing Kioxia/Sandisk memory-capacity thesis.

Evidence: primary SK hynix newsroom (2026-08-28) https://news.skhynix.com/en/groundbreaking-ceremony-in-indiana/ ; independent Reuters (2026-08-27) https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/sk-hynix-holds-groundbreaking-ceremony-4-billion-indiana-ai-chip-packaging-2026-08-27/ ; U.S. Senator Todd Young release (2026-08-27) https://www.young.senate.gov/newsroom/press-releases/senator-young-attends-sk-hynix-groundbreaking-ceremony-in-west-lafayette/ .

Conviction: +0.87 that HBM supply remains structurally tight into 2030 and that packaging/localization is a distinct constraint worth modeling. Caveat: management guidance is not independent demand data; capex can overshoot, schedules can slip, and new Samsung/Micron capacity could compress the shortage sooner.

First-order: supports sustained HBM pricing power/capex and U.S. packaging investment. Second-order: AI infrastructure graph should distinguish wafer capacity, HBM stack capacity, advanced packaging/test, geographic concentration, subsidy/CHIPS support, customer offtake, and utilization. Alpha test: monitor cleanroom milestones, tool move-in, packaging yields, HBM contract pricing, supplier lead times, and customer prepayments versus stated shortage duration.

What would falsify this: major HBM spot/contract price compression with improving lead times before 2030; material Indiana delays/cuts; substantial new competing capacity eliminating tightness; or hyperscaler/accelerator demand decelerating enough that HBM utilization falls despite announced capacity. No execution authority is attached to this message.
